Together, they built the magical city of Cardia. Today, life in the city is flourishing. Yet four factions are struggling for power: the Rebellion from the swamp, the scholars from the Academy , the Guild with their mechanical contraptions, and the Dynasty, descendants of the adventurer. Whoever wins the powerful signet rings, and thus the favour of the factions, becomes the next ruler of Cardia. Play your cards right and outsmart your opponent! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 3 End of Game 3.1 Abilities 4 Variations 4.1 Deck I vs. Deck II 4.2 Locations Overview Duel for Cardia is a little like "Love Letter" but for two players. Each player has an identical deck of 16 cards. Each card has a number and a special ability or effect. The players each play one card and duel. The card with the higher number wins a Signet Ring. The card that does not win activates an ability that may change the outcome of this or or other encounters. The player who collects 5 Signet Rings first wins the game. Gameplay During each encounter, each player plays a single card from their hand face down. Both cards are revealed simultaneously. The card that has the higher number wins one Signet Ring. The card with the lower number activates its ability. On a tie, no Signet Ring is awarded and neither ability is activated. The game moves onto the next encounter, but the previous encounter's cards remain in place. Abilities may affect the winner of the current encounter, previous encounters, or future encounters, or have ongoing effects. BGA defaults to playing two games. The winner of the best 2 out of 3 games wins. Since cards are activated simultaneously, the accounting of Signet Rings is not determined until all cards are resolved. If both players have 5, the game continues until a resolved encounter breaks the tie. End of Game There are three ways the game can end. If a player has at least 5 Signet Rings, that player wins. If a player cannot play a card, the other player wins. A card ability activates and causes one player to win. Abilities Only the ability of the lower card is activated. The ability of the higher card is ignored. There are two types of abilities: instant (lightning bolt) and ongoing (∞). Instant abilities are resolved once and only once. Ongoing abilities stay in effect for all encounters that take place after it is resolved. They don't affect past encounters. An "ongoing" symbol is placed on the card to indicate the ability is in effect. Some abilities change the influence of other cards. When this happens, the corresponding duel is re-evaluated. Signet Rings can change sides or be removed in the event of a tie. Important! When a Signet Ring changes sides, the ability on the lower card does not activate . Abilities cannot be retroactively invoked. Variations Deck I vs. Deck II Deck I has more cards that affect the current encounter or future encounters. Deck II has more cards that change the influence of other cards. Locations When creating a game table, you can optionally select a location. Each location has a rule that applies to the entire game. Descriptions can be found when selecting the location in table setup. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] It's not bad, but soon the game revolves entirely around the special abilities getting activated, more than the numbers themselves. Especially since you have a limited handsize the whole time. Which kinda kills off the mindgames and second-guessing, it's more about the rush of which special gets activated next. It's not thematic like Radlands, not complex like Battle Line, but neither is it simple and psychological like Hol's der Geier. It kinda does nothing amazing.

[Rating: 3/10] Literally nothing new. So, even if it works, why should I play it? Why should I BUY it?

[Rating: 3/10] Ok-ish game that rewards card counting and advanced knowledge of the deck. Tries to get by based based on rewarding feeling cardplay moments but there's seemingly a lack of skillful play to make it feel truly rewarding. It reminded me of Riftforce but less interesting.

[Rating: 3/10] Graphics and mechanism gokd, but Polish translation terrible. Probably will look for an English edition

[Rating: 4/10] Quirky little game - I appreciate the rub between winning vs. abilities, but overall it just felt kind of boring. It also didn't feel like I had that interesting of decisions to make.

[Rating: 4/10] Not enough decisions. You play a card and hope for your opponent to play weaker/stronger one. I like the "higher gets point, lower gets effect" mechanism, but the outcome is too unpredictable when both play the card simultaneously. Feels like a bluffing game.
